result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with modern safety features including continental crosswalks and green-painted bike lanes. While visibility is high and infrastructure is in good condition, the wide roadway geometry and lack of physical separation for cyclists and pedestrians increase exposure risks.

hazards.name: Wide intersection geometry
hazards.description: The wide radius of the intersection increases the distance pedestrians must travel while exposed to traffic and may encourage higher vehicle turning speeds.

hazards.name: Unprotected bike lanes
hazards.description: The bike lanes are marked with paint only, providing no physical protection from motor vehicle encroachment.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and sides of the roadway

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the corners to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised median or refuge island in the center of the crossing to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lanes
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing painted bike lanes with physical barriers such as bollards or concrete curbs to enhance cyclist safety.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a residential setting with continuous sidewalks but lacks dedicated pedestrian crossing infrastructure. While a traffic signal is present, the absence of marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals, combined with sightline obstructions from parked cars, creates a moderately risky environment for walking.

hazards.name: Lack of marked pedestrian crosswalks
hazards.description: Pedestrians lack a designated, high-visibility path across the intersection, increasing the risk of conflicts with vehicles.

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb near the intersection corners can hide pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility zebra-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight before they enter the roadway.

result.summary: The urban environment features basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, traffic signals, and marked crosswalks. However, the wide roadway and lack of physical separation for the bike lane create a high-exposure environment for non-motorized users.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians are exposed to traffic for a significant duration due to the width of the intersection without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Main intersection crossing in the center background

hazards.name: Unprotected Bike Lane
hazards.description: The bike lane is only separated by paint, offering no physical protection from motor vehicles in a high-traffic area.
hazards.location_in_image: Green painted lane on the left side of the roadway

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Add physical barriers such as bollards or a raised curb to separate the bike lane from motor vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade standard parallel line markings to continental or ladder style for better visibility to approaching motorists.

result.summary: The image shows a wide concrete sidewalk leading to a high-visibility green and white crosswalk at a signalized intersection. While basic infrastructure like traffic lights and marked crossings are present, the environment is somewhat industrial with utility poles obstructing the sidewalk path.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Multiple signal and utility poles are located in the middle of the sidewalk, creating obstacles for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids or visual impairments.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signals (walk/don't walk) are visible at this signalized intersection, which may lead to crossing uncertainty.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Clear Sidewalk Path
interventions.description: Relocate utility and signal poles to the furniture zone at the edge of the sidewalk to ensure a continuous, unobstructed clear path for pedestrians.
